title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 392
paragraphs: In the reign of Amasis, Egypt is said to have been more prosperous than at any previous time, both from what the river gave to the land and from what the land gave to its people. The country at that time contained twenty thousand inhabited cities. It was Amasis who established the law that every Egyptian must appear once a year before the governor of his district and declare his means of livelihood. Anyone who failed to do so, or could not prove he lived by honest means, was punished by death. The Athenian Solon brought this law from Egypt and established it at Athens. It is an excellent law, and I hope it stays in force forever.
